standard_prerequisites.name: Picard group of a ringed site is the first cohomology of the sheaf of invertible functions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma labelled sites-cohomology-lemma-h1-invertible (canonical Stacks tag 040E); invoked at proof lines 2295-2298
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification turning the long exact sequence of units into the displayed sequence of Picard groups.

core_obligations: Identify the two etale sites: use that X_etale = X'_etale for a thickening of algebraic spaces, citing the equivalence lemma and the surrounding discussion, so that the sequence of sheaves on X_etale may be used to compare invariants of X and X' (proof lines 2285-2287).

Form the exponential sequence: for a first order thickening X contained in X' with ideal sheaf I, the map sending a local section f of I to the invertible section 1 + f of O_{X'} is well defined because I^2 = 0 and gives the short exact sequence 0 -> I -> O_{X'}^* -> O_X^* -> 0 of sheaves of abelian groups on X_etale (proof lines 2288-2294).

Read off the sequence: taking the long exact cohomology sequence and replacing the first cohomology of the sheaves of invertible functions by Picard groups via the cited identification gives the displayed sequence 0 -> H^0(X, I) -> H^0(X', O_{X'}^*) -> H^0(X, O_X^*) -> H^1(X, I) -> Pic(X') -> Pic(X) -> H^2(X, I) (proof lines 2288-2298).
proof_roadmap: Use X_etale = X'_etale to be able to work with sheaves on one site (proof lines 2285-2287).
Write down the exponential short exact sequence of units attached to the square-zero ideal sheaf (proof lines 2288-2294).
Identify the H^1 of the units with the Picard groups to obtain the displayed exact sequence (proof lines 2295-2298).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts a canonical exact sequence 0 -> H^0(X, I) -> H^0(X', O_{X'}^*) -> H^0(X, O_X^*) -> H^1(X, I) -> Pic(X') -> Pic(X) -> H^2(X, I) for a first order thickening X contained in X' of algebraic spaces over a scheme S, with ideal sheaf I (statement lines 2266-2281). Two steps carry the content: the identification of the small etale sites of X and X' for a thickening, which is what allows a single site to be used at all, and the exponential map f -> 1 + f from the square-zero ideal sheaf into the units (proof lines 2285-2294). The remaining step replaces H^1 of the units by the Picard groups and is a citation. The claim is H2: two structural inputs and one cited identification.
